clauses.reason: The title and enacting words of EO 11003 state the order's subject, assigning emergency preparedness functions to the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Agency, and the authority under which the President acted, including Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1958; they operate only through the numbered sections that follow, so they ended with the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11003: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (11), "Executive Order No. 11003 of February 16, 1962.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 1 of EO 11003 directs the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Agency to prepare national emergency plans and develop preparedness programs covering the emergency management of the Nation's civil airports, civil aviation operating facilities, civil aviation services, and civil aircraft other than air carrier aircraft, designed to develop a state of readiness in those areas for all conditions of national emergency. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11003: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (11), "Executive Order No. 11003 of February 16, 1962.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 2 of EO 11003 assigns the Administrator transportation functions, set out in lettered paragraphs on national program guidance, operations, priorities and allocations, requirements and claimancy. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11003: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (11), "Executive Order No. 11003 of February 16, 1962.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 3 of EO 11003 directs the Administrator, in consonance with the national civil defense plans, programs and operations of the Department of Defense under Executive Order No. 10952, to carry out functions set out in lettered paragraphs on professional training, facilities protection, monitoring, decontamination, damage assessment, and salvage and rehabilitation. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11003: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (11), "Executive Order No. 11003 of February 16, 1962.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 4 of EO 11003 directs the Administrator, within the framework of Federal research objectives, to supervise or conduct research directly concerned with carrying out emergency preparedness responsibilities, to designate representatives for necessary ad hoc or task force groups, and to provide advice and assistance to other agencies in planning for research in areas involving the Agency's interest. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11003: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (11), "Executive Order No. 11003 of February 16, 1962.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 5 of EO 11003 sets the guidance by which the Administrator, in carrying out the functions assigned in the order, is to be guided: interagency cooperation, Presidential coordination (the Director of the Office of Emergency Planning is to advise and assist the President in determining policy for the performance of functions under the order and in coordinating them with the total national preparedness program), and emergency planning (emergency plans, programs and organization are to be developed as an integral part of the continuing activities of the Agency on the basis that it will have responsibility for carrying them out during an emergency, and the Administrator is to be prepared to implement all appropriate plans developed under the order). It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11003: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (11), "Executive Order No. 11003 of February 16, 1962.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 6 of EO 11003 provides that nothing in the order is to be construed as conferring authority under Title III of the Federal Civil Defense Act of 1950, as amended, or otherwise, to put into effect any emergency plan, procedure, policy, program, or course of action prepared or developed pursuant to the order, and states that such authority is reserved to the President. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11003: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (11), "Executive Order No. 11003 of February 16, 1962.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 7 of EO 11003 authorizes the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Agency to redelegate within the Agency the functions assigned to him in the order. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11003: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (11), "Executive Order No. 11003 of February 16, 1962.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

The first sentence of Section 8 of EO 11003 provides that, to the extent of any inconsistency between the provisions of any prior order and the provisions of this order, the latter controls. That rule was a continuing command and stayed in force while the order did. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11003: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (11), "Executive Order No. 11003 of February 16, 1962.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

The remaining sentence of Section 8 of EO 11003 revokes Emergency Preparedness Order No. 3, issued earlier by the Director of the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization. It is a one-time act that was complete when the order was issued; nothing in it continued afterwards. The held text of EO 11003, signed John F. Kennedy on February 16, 1962 at the White House, carries the revocation, so it was performed on that date (no later event is needed). The order as a whole was later revoked on 1969-10-28, but this one-time act had been completed on 1962-02-16.

research_rationale:
EO 11003 (1962-02-16; Assigning emergency preparedness functions to the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Agency) was read in full from the held Federal Register text (27 FR 1540, Federal Register of 1962-02-20), whose file also contains neighbouring material; the order was delimited by its heading and the John F. Kennedy signature line. The dossier's machine segmentation, which cuts sections into lettered fragments and repeats some, was replaced by 10 scopes: one for the enacting words and one for each numbered section. Section 8 is split in two: its first sentence (precedence over inconsistent prior orders) and its closing sentence, which revokes Emergency Preparedness Order No. 3, issued earlier by the Director of the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization. Its own terms contain no end date, expiry or termination condition. It ended on 1969-10-28 by express revocation in EO 11490, Sec. 3015, item (11), cited from the American Presidency Project transcription (APP node 255823; page record checked: heading, date and text hash agree with the held text) and read for corroboration in the Federal Register print of 34 FR 17567 onward (OCR text), which lists the same order. No amendment, suspension or other instrument naming it is held besides EO 11490, which revokes it. The only other held file naming it by number, besides EO 11490, is the text file of EO 11002, which ends with this order's heading (a neighbouring page) and is not a later instrument. The selected machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register catalog) are coverage statements read before use; they are leads, not independent review.

savings.reason: Item (11) of Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 revokes EO 11003. In the held American Presidency Project transcription, Sec. 3014 reads: "Except as provided by Section 3015, nothing in this order shall be deemed to derogate from any now existing assignment of functions to any department or agency or officer thereof made by statute, Executive order, or Presidential directives, including Memoranda." Because Sec. 3014 begins with that exception, it does not preserve the revoked order. The end source span cited for this claim runs from "SECTION 501. Functions." through Sec. 3015, that is Parts 5 through 30 of EO 11490. I read Sec. 3014 and Sec. 3015; I did not read the other Parts to decide whether any of them carries this order's commands forward, so no transfer or accrual is claimed and the state is none_after_bounded_search.
